The most positive aspect of the course was that it challenged us with unfamiliar projects and pushed us to adapt to difficult situations. However, beyond that, I struggled to find many positive sides to the experience. Our first major assignment was a “living music video” project in TouchDesigner, a program that most of us had no experience with. While the concept initially sounded interesting, the process quickly became frustrating because we lacked both technical knowledge and proper guidance. When we asked questions, the answers were often simply “ask GPT,” and even then the responses we received were usually not helpful. At some point, the project stopped feeling educational and became more exhausting than productive. I believe education should involve learning from experienced people, not only receiving feedback after struggling alone.

Another major issue was the inconsistency throughout the semester. The department emphasizes solving problems independently, but when we genuinely tried to learn the correct approaches, there was rarely clear guidance available. At the same time, expectations for project quality remained very high, which made the uncertainty stressful for both individuals and teams. Later in the semester, we were suddenly given a second film option instead of another TouchDesigner project, and we mainly chose it to avoid TouchDesigner rather than out of genuine interest. We wanted more varied and real-world-oriented projects like the music video and documentary assignments from previous semesters. Overall, the constant changes and unclear direction made the semester discouraging. At times, the management style of the department reminds me of Fenerbahçe: there are constant changes and new ideas, but the long-term direction and results remain unclear. Despite all of this, being able to complete both projects still felt like a major achievement for us.

Ufuk hoca is one of the greatest instructors that I have encountered during my college life. I believe that only a number of instructors in the department are successfully capable of building a bridge between the academic aspects of a field and the field work and he is one of them. The fact that he has such a rich background in the industry and is still actively working in the field makes him capable of providing information to the students about what is going on in the industry and such. In this department, I have observed several times that some instructors are teaching courses based on their personal likings. For instance, if we are taking a course that involves filmmaking, I believe that we should be learning about how to make films that are currently being produced (such as blockbusters) since we are paying a great deal of money to this school and we expect to be equipped enough to work in such films to make a good living. But instead, most instructors tend to spend hours on teaching independent art films that are watched by only a handful of people and therefore, are unable to provide a well enough income to its producers. Ufuk Önen, on the other hand, is teaching about how big names in the industry are currently working and what is required so we would be able to either be one of those names or work with them in the future.
